scope: AI visual audit of broad graphic inventory, order, layout and selected discrepancies; no phonetic or semantic reading and no expert palaeographic authentication.
global_findings: All selected IDs can be located in the primary CISI1 scan. Impression photographs match the normalized visual orientation; originals are mirrored.
Published images broadly support the presence and order of the recorded graphic shapes, but small hatching and compound segmentation often cannot be independently decided from the scans.
Exact candidate compatibility is a cross-catalogue check, not an estimated transcription accuracy. Incompatible strings may be valid alternate segmentations or incomplete crosswalks.

The first blind descriptive pass made some grouping/count mistakes. Preserve it as evidence of visual uncertainty, not an authoritative retranscription. Post-comparison corrections are explicitly recorded below.
This sample covers Mohenjo-daro seals with unicorn imagery and cannot authenticate the full corpus, its archaeological metadata, or other artifact types.

rows.note: Impression U+central hanging element, crossed person-like form and rectangle with internal teeth agree in order with P316/P011/P270 and Wells706/140/632. Internal U element is a tapered closed shape in the photo; the coarse schema calls it a stroke.
Wheel, raised-arm person, five tall strokes and paired leaves on T stem agree. The pitchfork/burden small-stroke count is not independently assigned a Wells allograph.
Seven broad groups agree. The looped people/plants and internal decoration should retain schema feature uncertainty despite clear aggregate compatibility.
Jar, three triangles, striped triangle, two short strokes and terminal small-top diamond agree. The small top diamond is rounded in the impression; Wells817 versus861 is not determined independently.

Six catalogue tokens agree. Blind pass grouped a tiny short stroke together with the adjacent tall stroke/U; it should not be used as a count validation. Mayig and Lipi separately encode full-height031 and half-height001 here.

Lipi has400/520/897 and marks completeY; Mayig has tree/triangle/lyre/P000. Three visible broad glyphs agree, but broken upper edge and P000 mean the Mayig sequence is not a clear transcription. Wells896 versus897 is a fine variant not adjudicated.
Leaf, tree, larger decorated leaf, two short strokes and small-top diamond agree. Small inner/top details remain limited by scan.

Primary impression clearly shows two adjacent grids. Mayig encodes two P268 grids each mapped toW615; Lipi encodes a singleW617 compound. Final primary form is an open caret on a stem, consistent with Mayig P217 tip_shape feature but its schema only listsW520, whereas Lipi usesW070. Do not classify the resulting length6 versus7 as a copying error.

The first blind pass mistook a jar-headed burden bearer for conjoined jars and grouped its appendages loosely. Exact Mayig/Lipi candidate compatibility and broad shape order hold; five catalogue tokens, not the six blind descriptive groups.
Jar, tree, square-on-stem, fish and three short strokes agree. Blind notes grouped adjacent tree/square and overcounted short strokes; no numeral-value conclusion should use that initial pass.
Six broad groups agree; primary detail supports fish/complex parenthesized fish-and-bird inventories, but fine internal bars remain an annotator decision.

Only second token is candidate incompatible: LipiW844 versus Mayig P352 listingW845. Primary has a complex paired-leaf shape; no independent844/845 decision from this scan. Eight catalogue tokens; the seven-group blind pass underestimated the count and cannot validate exact segmentation of the final groups.
Triangle, three distinct fish-like signs, jar and angularH agree. Horizontal crossbar, whiskers and hat distinguish the three catalogue fish classes; no phonetic equivalence inferred.
Three catalogue tokens agree; first is a jar-headed burden bearer, which the blind pass described too literally as conjoined jars.
Triangle, three full-height strokes, U+central stroke and single full-height stroke agree. This is a useful visual example of033/705 adjacency, not evidence for the meaning of705.

Only third token differs: LipiW002 two short strokes versus Mayig P145/W032 two full-height strokes. Enlarged impression shows two strokes occupying the upper portion of the text band; this favors the short-stroke description, but no source transcription is edited. Seven-token inventory otherwise agrees. Blind first pass incorrectly counted three.

Primary has two visual rows and an incomplete upper text. LipiN/multiline agrees with that. Mayig carries P000 twice but zero default damage/uncertainty and line1 for all tokens. This exposed the need to exclude P000 explicitly; it cannot count among clear complete faces.
Jar, three-headed person, comb/pitchfork, fish, two short strokes and small-top diamond agree in visual order.
Six broad tokens agree. Fine corner-stroke features of first fish and the inner branch count of leaf are not independently scored from the scan.

LipiW832 is leaf+inner vertical stroke; Mayig P368 lists leaf+dot andW808/809/810. The enlarged primary inner element looks elongated, favoring the stroke description, but photo relief/shadow can affect shape. Keep discrepant observation rather than asserting a corrected allograph.

Four catalogue tokens agree. The many short vertical elements belong to the arms of compoundU/W772; onlyW002 is a separate two-stroke token. Blind first pass treated these decorations as a separate numeric cluster and should not be used for numeral analysis.

Lipi hasW900 parenthesis andW320 arch/bar shape versus Mayig candidatesW920 andW322–325. Broad five-group inventory agrees. Enlarged impression shows a small middle nub on curved stroke and several lower bars under arch; catalogue variant definitions are required to decide exact codes.
Tree and six short strokes in two rows of three agree. Counting the strokes is secure in this image; treating the whole stack as one sign is the catalogue segmentation.

rows.status: schema crosswalk omission or variant difference
rows.note: LipiW502 is a decorated triangle; Mayig P207 description says no decoration and listsW490, but includes a decoration feature allowing a tree. Primary clearly has internal marks in the triangle. This supports a decorated triangle and exposes a coarse-schema correspondence limit rather than a necessarily wrong transcription.
Triangle, crossed fish, a small bent-pair sign and parallel bent strokes agree. The blind pass called the bent pair two short straight bars; they should retain the distinction encoded byP120/W060.
